verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Lean states the identity for the cut-off wave, with the cutoff carried on the right-hand side: `C(η W_0) = ε · mask² · T_{0,*}` rather than `C(W_0) = ε T_{0,*}`. The two differ only by the factor mask², which is forced by the choice recorded under eq-7.24 (Lean's `amplitude` absorbs the cutoff into the coefficient). The recovery is routine and is already available inside the repository: C is quadratic in the wave and the mask is constant in the two averaging variables (Y, theta), so it pulls out of `doubleAverage` as mask²; equivalently `weighted_columns_reconstruct` has `mask` as a free real parameter, and taking mask = 1 gives exactly `∑_j a_j² H i j = ε T i`, which is (7.26) read columnwise, C(W_0)_i = ε · (T_{0,*})_i. The covariance functional C is `doubleAverage` of the radial component times the i-th tangential component (indices `0` and `i.succ` of a Fin 3 velocity), matching the paper's angular-then-torus average of the rθ and rz stresses; the Lean target is `PrimaryTargetBounds.actualTarget`, which is the normalized target carrying the (Q/q)^{A+1/2} factor (the companion `PartitionedCovariance.chartTarget`, line 940, states that factor explicitly with `velocityExponent h = 1/2 + h`). I did not verify that `actualTarget` and `chartTarget` agree pointwise.
